newsitem.title: JAPAN: Early Asia cash Brent surges, wet markets sleep.
newsitem.headline: Early Asia cash Brent surges, wet markets sleep.

text.p: Cash Brent values in surged in early Asia on Tuesday in response to new U.N.-Iraqi tensions and widespread short covering that followed in Western markets on Monday.
Notional values for August cash Brent were assessed at $18.00/18.10 per barrel, marking a 20 cent gain over day-earlier levels.

In addition to the normal jitters accompanying OPEC's semi-annual meeting in Vienna, markets gained on news of Iraqi refusals to allow U.N. weapons inspectors access to sensitive sites and a U.N. threat to respond with additional sanctions.
NYMEX WTI values continued to climb in out-of-hours ACCESS trade, with the August contract reaching $19.32 in early Asia following New York's close of $19.14.
Asian physical markets were indifferent to the news, with some continued Japanese utility buying of regional heavy grades for direct crude burning marking the only discussed activity.
Middle East grade markets still saw lacklustre buying interest for the month of August, traders said.
"There just doesn't seem to be that much demand out there," said one trader.
Traders said Oman was likely to change hands within the week but that Abu Dhabi grades would likely remain inactive.
